title: Build your Plunge city by unclogging toilets
author: Famous-Stable-8092
selftext:
I've been making a small browser clicker game called Toilet Plunge with an AI assistant. You unclog toilets, buy better plungers, hire workers, buy factories, set up plumbing services and much more, all while you build your Plunge city and win achievements and rewards along the way. 

The process went roughly like this:

1. Built a small first version with the free GPT and Claude models, a quick game you could finish in one sitting.  
2. Decided I wanted the game to last much longer without making the tapping feel slow.  
4. Went back and forth: changed the pacing, played and tested the game, adjust again.  
5. Added fixes along the way, like save functionality and performance fixes.

The performance issues from the visual effects were a struggle until I tried Opus 5.5, before that I was using the free AI models from Claude and GPT. 

I first tried limiting with how many fingers you can tap on the phone to improve the performance but now it works fine even with multiple fingers tapping at the same time. 

Honestly I even started building this from scratch with Unity to achieve the native performance and responsive layout using Unity’s anchors but that will take long time. 

With Opus 5.5 I fixed the performance issues using basic prompts like: The game is lagging and is slow when clicking with multiple fingers at the same time.

The responsive layout was also done by Opus 5.5. I tried testing it on multiple devices and looks okay. 

I plan to do more thorough testing of the responsive layout with online services. 

Feel free to check the game, it’s free to play in the browser: [https://toiletplunge.com](https://toiletplunge.com/)

Curious how you guys here playtest long games made with AI regarding the performance and responsive layout on different devices.
